description: Code smell definitions for relation mapping

SMELL-01.name: Long Method
SMELL-01.description: Method contains too many lines of code (typically >20-30 lines)
symptoms: Requires inline comments to explain sections

SMELL-02.name: Long Parameter List
SMELL-02.description: More than 3-4 parameters in a method

SMELL-03.name: Primitive Obsession
SMELL-03.description: Use of primitives instead of small objects for simple tasks

SMELL-04.name: Large Class
SMELL-04.description: Class contains too many fields, methods, or lines of code

SMELL-05.name: Data Clumps
SMELL-05.description: Different parts of code contain identical groups of variables
symptoms: Same group of parameters in multiple methods

SMELL-06.name: Switch Statements
SMELL-06.description: Complex switch/case or long if-else chains

SMELL-07.name: Data Class
SMELL-07.description: Class contains only fields with getters and setters but no meaningful behavior
symptoms: Methods are mostly getters and setters
No behavior or business logic in the class

SMELL-08.name: Temporary Field
SMELL-08.description: Object field set only in certain circumstances, leaving it empty or null the rest of the time
symptoms: Field is only set in specific code paths
Field is null or empty under normal conditions
Code checks whether field is set before using it

SMELL-09.name: Shotgun Surgery
SMELL-09.description: Single change requires many small changes to many different classes
symptoms: Hard to find all places to change

SMELL-10.name: Divergent Change
SMELL-10.description: One class commonly changed in different ways for different reasons
symptoms: Different methods change for different features

SMELL-11.name: Lazy Class
SMELL-11.description: Class that does too little and does not justify its existence
symptoms: Very few methods or lines of code
Class is nearly empty or trivial
Could be merged into another class

SMELL-12.name: Speculative Generality
SMELL-12.description: Unused abstraction created for anticipated future needs that never materialise
symptoms: Abstract class or interface with only one implementation
Class is defined but never or rarely used

SMELL-13.name: Duplicate Code
SMELL-13.description: Same code structure appears in multiple places

SMELL-14.name: Middle Man
SMELL-14.description: Class delegates most of its work to another class, adding no value of its own
symptoms: Class can be removed without losing behaviour

SMELL-19.name: Inappropriate Intimacy
SMELL-19.description: Two classes access each other's private parts more than necessary, creating excessive coupling
symptoms: Classes access each other's private fields or methods
Excessive coupling making changes in one class affect the other

SMELL-15.name: Parallel Inheritance Hierarchies
SMELL-15.description: Every time you create a subclass for one class you find yourself needing to create a subclass for another
symptoms: Two class hierarchies mirror each other
Adding a subclass in one hierarchy requires adding one in another
Class name prefixes are the same in both hierarchies

SMELL-16.name: Comments
SMELL-16.description: Comment used as deodorant to explain confusing code rather than to convey intent that code cannot express
symptoms: Long comment block explaining what the code does
Comment that would be unnecessary if the code were clearer
TODO or FIXME comments persisting without resolution

SMELL-17.name: Dead Code
SMELL-17.description: Code that is no longer used or reachable and could be safely removed
symptoms: Unreachable code after a return or throw
Variables, methods, or classes that are never referenced
Commented-out code left in the codebase

SMELL-18.name: Feature Envy
SMELL-18.description: Method accesses data of another object more than its own
symptoms: Method uses many getters from another class
Method is more interested in other class than its own

SMELL-20.name: Message Chains
SMELL-20.description: Client asks object for another object, which asks for another, etc.

SMELL-21.name: God Object
SMELL-21.description: Class that knows and does too much, centralising an excessive number of responsibilities

SMELL-22.name: Refused Bequest
SMELL-22.description: Subclass inherits methods or data it does not need or want from its parent
symptoms: Subclass inherits methods or data it does not use
Subclass overrides inherited behaviour to do nothing or throw
Base class carries baggage that only some subclasses need

SMELL-23.name: Alternative Classes with Different Interfaces
SMELL-23.description: Two classes perform identical or similar functions but have different method signatures
symptoms: Two classes do similar things but have different method names
Classes could be used interchangeably but lack a common interface
Clients must know which class to use and adapt to each
